Pradesh on 11 July, 2024
Author: Ninala Jayasurya

Bench: Ninala Jayasurya  APHC010326342015  IN THE HIGH COURT OF ANDHRA PRADESH  AT AMARAVATI [3209]
 (Special Original Jurisdiction)
 THURSDAY, THE ELEVENTH DAY OF JULY  TWO THOUSAND AND TWENTY FOUR  PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE NINALA JAYASURYA  WRIT PETITION NO: 23070 of 2015 Between:-
Chitlu Chiranjeeva Rao  .... Petitioner  And The State of Andhra Pradesh and others.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF ANDHRA PRADESH  AT AMARAVATI [3209]
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ..... Respondents Counsel for the petitioner : Mr.P.Lakshmana Rao Counsel for the respondents : G.P. for Land Acquistion

The Court made the following:
ORDER:
Questioning the inaction of the respondents in referring the matter to Civil Court as illegal, arbitrary etc., and contrary to Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and also the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the present Writ Petition is filed.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
NJS,J WP_21535_2015 Chitlu Chiranjeeva Rao S/O Late ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11438904/
1 2) Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Also heard the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the 4th respondent.

3) Referring to the averments made in the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petition, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that an extent of Ac.3-57 cents, Ac.1-36 cents, Ac.0-91 cents and Ac.0-22 cents situated in Sy.Nos.49/2, 50/2B,, 52/2B and 53/1A respectively of Chiguruvalasa Village, Sarbujjili Mandal, Srikakulam District, the petitioner's ancestral property was acquired pursuant to the acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act-1894").

He submits that as the petitioner was aggrieved by the fixation, the compensation amounts were received under protest and the petitioner requested the authorities to refer the matter to the competent Civil Court under Section 18 of the Act-1894.

He submits that though the petitioner made an application in this regard on 16.02.2010, no steps were taken by the authorities and in those circumstances the petitioner was constrained to file the instant Writ Petition.

4) Learned counsel submits that while the petitioner's request to refer the matter to the Civil Court under Section 18 of the Act-1894 was pending consideration, the new Land Acquisition Act viz., the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Act-2013") came into operation and in terms of the provisions of the Act-2013, the petitioner is entitled for NJS,J WP_21535_2015 enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Due to inaction on the part of the official respondents he submits that the petitioner is subjected to great hardship and irreparable loss and unless the relief sought for in the present Writ Petition is granted,
the petitioner would suffer serious prejudice.
Making the said submissions, the learned counsel urges for granting the relief as prayed for.
5) On the other hand, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition, made submissions with reference to the averments made in the counter affidavit filed by the 4th respondent.

She submits that as stated in para-5 of the counter affidavit, the petitioner after a long lapse of about seven (07) years, made an application dated 16.02.2010 to the 5th respondent with a request to refer the matter to the Civil Court under Section 18 of the Act-1894 for determination of amount of compensation.

She submits that the District Level Committee under the Chairmanship of District Collector approved the compensation in respect of the petitioner's lands on 08.01.2004, the petitioner agreed to the same and signed on the report of negotiations committee.

Referring to Ex.P1 she submits that the petitioner did not file his application within time i.e., Six (06) weeks for referring the matter to the Civil Court as required under Section 18 of the Act-1894, that the allegations made in the affidavit are not true and without any valid basis.
She also opposes the contention that the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the Act-2013.
Making the said submissions, she urges for dismissal of the Writ Petition.
NJS,J WP_21535_2015 6) This Court has considered the submissions made and perused the material on record.

It is not in dispute that the subject matter land was acquired in the year 2003 and the petitioner made an application to the 5th respondent instead of to the 4th respondent i.e., the Special Deputy Collector,
Vamsadhara Project / Land Acquisition Officer in the year 2010, seeking reference under Section 1B Chitlu Chiranjeeva Rao S/O Late ... vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11438904/
2 of the Act, 1894.

entities.text:
Special Deputy Collector,
Vamsadhara Project / Land Acquisition Officer
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: No reasons are forthcoming for the abnormal delay of about seven (07) years.
Be that as it may.

As per the specific case of the 4th respondent set out in the counter affidavit, it would appear that the petitioner agreed for the compensation as fixed by the District Level Negotiations Committee, headed by the District Collector and no reply affidavit is filed traversing the counter affidavit averments.
That apart, the 4th respondent had taken a specific plea that the petitioner had not filed the application for reference within six weeks as contemplated under the provisions of the Act, 1894.
For the reasons best known to the petitioner, he did not choose to file reply affidavit.

Thus, the contentions raised on behalf of the 4th respondent remain unrebutted and non-denial of the specific assertions made in the counter affidavit, tantamount to admission of the same.
7)
In the aforementioned facts and circumstances and on due consideration of the matter, this Court see no reason to exercise the jurisdiction vested under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
NJS,J WP_21535_2015 8) Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
9) Consequently, the Miscellaneous Applications pending, if any, shall also stand dismissed.
NINALA JAYASURYA, J Date: 11.07.2024 SSV NJS,J WP_21535_2015
